key_insight: Orthogonalized momentum can fail on nonsmooth convex problems when momentum is fixed, but becomes reliable when momentum is made adaptive and paired with vanishing step sizes.
engineering_relevance: For matrix-valued optimization in deep learning, this work suggests when Muon-style updates are unsafe and proposes MAGD as a practical drop-in alternative with provable convergence guarantees.
method: Analyze Muon under locally Lipschitz/nonsmooth objectives using generalized derivatives compatible with backpropagation.
Construct a counterexample showing fixed-momentum Muon can miss the global optimum from almost all initializations, even with bounded iterates.
Introduce MAGD, which mixes orthogonalized momentum with gradients based on relative progress and prove asymptotic convergence plus an optimal dimension-dependent convex rate.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on synthetic problems, image classification, and LLM pretraining, supporting MAGD’s practical performance.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on boundedness/regularity assumptions and, for reliability, an adaptive momentum schedule with vanishing step size rather than a fixed-momentum Muon update.
